newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus won't keep up drastic rise-MOF.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus won't keep up drastic rise-MOF.

text.p: Japan's trade surplus is unlikely to continue to grow drastically in the medium to longer term, a Ministry of Finance (MOF) official said on Monday.

The ministry official said there was a continuation of structural changes which had been occurring in Japan since 1993, such as manufacturers' expansion of production overseas, an increase in imports of finished products and deregulation.
"I don't think the trade surplus will continue to expand drastically as a trend," he said.
Asked about the impact of the consumption tax increase on trade data, he said: "We can still see the impact of the sales tax increase on cars and clothing."
In its calculation of the value of imports and exports for July, the ministry used an exchange rate of 114.09 yen, compared with 109.60 yen a year ago.

"We cannot deny the impact of currency fluctuations on trade movements, but there are other factors that affect trade, such as economic conditions both at home and abroad. It is difficult to say what impact the currency fluctuations alone had on the trade data," he said.
The ministry announced earlier on Monday that Japan's trade surplus rose for the fourth successive month in July, surging 69.7 percent from a year earlier to 849.08 billion yen.

The customs-cleared trade surplus with the United States, often a source of friction, jumped 35.7 percent in July from a year earlier to 420.55 billion yen. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.
